result.title: Hint-Informed Self-Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation
result.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables. The first two authors contributed equally
result.summary: Reasoning segmentation requires identifying the target referred to by a query among visually similar objects, yet trajectory-level rewards cannot directly indicate which tokens provide relevant visual evidence. We propose Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), which uses target-disambiguation evidence for token-level credit assignment. An external model generates Segment Hints offline from training images, queries, and ground-truth target annotations, organizing target identity, discriminative attributes, confusable objects, and anchoring paths. A hint-conditioned exponential moving average teacher scores the student's own trajectories, and HISD computes the teacher-to-student evidence ratio over a token support set to adjust only the magnitudes of positive group-relative advantages, leaving nonpositive advantages unchanged. This design encourages concise reasoning while retaining the information needed for target disambiguation, and the student requires neither hints nor a teacher at inference. Under a unified training protocol, HISD improves ReasonSeg test gIoU and cIoU over our reproduction of DPAD by 3.00 and 3.55 percentage points, respectively. Across the five evaluated splits of ReasonSeg and the RefCOCO family, HISD achieves higher segmentation metrics than this baseline and reduces the average token count of valid reasoning spans by 80.17 to 91.83 percent.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Hint-Informed Self-Distillation（HISD），在 reasoning segmentation 中利用外部模型离线生成的 Segment Hints（目标身份、判别属性、易混对象、锚定路径），以 hint 条件化的 EMA 教师对学生自身轨迹上的 token 支持集计算教师-学生证据比，仅缩放正群组相对优势的幅度，从而实现 token 级信用分配，并大幅压缩有效推理跨度长度。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「贡献分配与监督」「视觉证据筛选」与推理长度成本：其 token 级证据比可能提供核查推理链是否真正依据判别性视觉证据的线索，但该方法属训练期辅助机制而非推理期状态生成，且压缩长度是否损失目标消歧需读原文核实。
